── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3 km
This week: 2.8 km over 1 run. Missed 2 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Came down with a cold on Tuesday that turned into a fever, 38.4 on Wednesday night. No fever since Friday but still coughing and blocked up."
Feeling: "Wiped out."
Asks: "Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Do not add the missed runs. …
Answers: (1) No to adding the two missed runs, and no to three runs next week. Do two. (2) Those missed sessions were short, easy walk-run days, and a week away does not undo the habit you built. … (3) Here is how to decide on Wed Sep 16: (4) Go if you have had no fever, the cough is easing and you feel close to normal. …
Safety flag: See a doctor if symptoms linger or change
Next week:
Mon: rest. No running, and keep the dog walk easy. You are still coughing and wiped out…
Tue: rest. Easy dog walk only. A second day off gives you an honest read on how you feel…
Wed: easy, 20 min, 2 min walk, then 6 x 1 min easy jog with 2 min walk between. Jog…
Thu: rest. Easy dog walk only. A day between runs lets you see how the legs and chest…
Fri: rest. Easy dog walk only, and aim for 7 hours of sleep. Sleep helps you recover…
Sat: easy, 21 min, 3 min walk, then 6 x 2 min easy run with 1 min walk between. Run only…
Sun: rest. Easy dog walk only. A rest day after the week's second run lets your body…
